title: The Birth Certificate Bond Theory — Here's What's Real and What Isn't
summary: A credit-and-business coach explains that the birth-certificate bond and secret account do not exist, then pivots to selling credit repair and business-entity coaching.

assertions.quote: the birth certificate didn't create a bond. It created a record
They don't create a separate corporate entity with a trading value
The courts have rejected these arguments. These accounts don't respond, and the filings don't produce results.
Birth certificates are filed with state vital statistics office. They are not registered with the SEC.

verdicts.note: CUSIPs identify registered securities; numbers on birth certificates are state file numbers, and no birth-certificate securities exist.

assertions.quote: reflect formatting traditions in legal typography.

verdicts.note: Courts and style manuals treat capitalisation as formatting; judges routinely hold it has no legal significance.
The court treats the all-caps duplicate name as a meaningless pseudolaw motif with no legal effect, grounds for refusing the filing.
The Tax Court held correspondence addressed in all capital letters is not invalid and the contrary 'fictional legal entity' argument is frivolous, i.e. the capitalisation has no legal effect.
Courts treat the capitalised name in their documents as simply identifying the defendant, though the source does not discuss typographic convention directly.

assertions.quote: your personal legal name will be separated from business liability, the way the system was designed to allow.

verdicts.note: LLCs and corporations do limit owner liability, but personal guarantees, veil-piercing and personal torts often reach the owner.
